messages:
Navya Patel: Hey team — first-week hiccup. My kubectl keeps switching contexts mid-session and my AWS SSO creds seem to expire every ~10m when I try to tail logs in namespace `redwood-app`. Anyone seen this? (mac M1, zsh)

Priya Singh: Hey Navya :wave: Which context are you on? Can you paste `kubectl config current-context` and `kubectl config get-contexts` (or `kubectl config view --minify --flatten`) so we can see the exec plugin output?

Navya Patel: Current context: `arn:aws:eks:us-west-2:123456789012:cluster/redwood-dev`
`kubectl config get-contexts` shows:
```
CURRENT   NAME                                      CLUSTER           AUTHINFO
*         arn:aws:eks:us-west-2:123456789012:cluster/redwood-dev   redwood-dev-cluster   arn:aws:eks:...-sso
          arn:aws:eks:us-west-2:123456789012:cluster/redwood-prod  redwood-prod-cluster  arn:aws:eks:...-sso
```
And the user entry is an `exec` block that calls `aws` (looks like aws sso). When I run `kubectl logs -f ...` it works for a few minutes then `error: You must re-authenticate (error: exec plugin has expired credentials)`.

Samir Chen: That sounds like the exec credential plugin issuing very short-lived creds. Try `aws sso login --profile redwood-dev` first and then re-run. If you're on mac M1, also make sure your `aws` binary is the one from our recommended distro (we've seen the brew binary behave oddly).

Miguel Torres: We also have a small helper script in the devex repo: `scripts/kube/login.sh` — it runs `aws sso login` and writes a stable per-user context `navya-redwood-dev` that pins the namespace. Try `./scripts/kube/login.sh navya-p` from the repo root.

Priya Singh: Short-term, I can also create a namespace-scoped ServiceAccount and give you `view` permissions in `redwood-app` so you don't hit cluster-wide RBAC issues. Do you want that, or would you rather fix SSO?

Navya Patel: My GitHub handle is `navya-p`. I tried `aws sso login` but it opens the browser and after auth I still see the same re-auth error ~8 minutes into streaming logs. Not sure why it drops mid-session.

Priya Singh: Two quick things: 1) create a named context that sets `namespace: redwood-app` so accidental context switches won't change your namespace, and 2) I'll grant you `view` in `redwood-app` so you can tail logs without needing cluster-admin perms. Run this locally to create a context alias (I'll create the server-side binding):
```
kubectl config set-context navya-redwood-app --cluster=redwood-dev --user=arn:aws:eks:us-west-2:123456789012:node/placeholder --namespace=redwood-app
kubectl config use-context navya-redwood-app
```
(I used a placeholder user; once your SSO creds are valid the `user` exec plugin will populate).

Priya Singh: Update: I created a RoleBinding in `redwood-app` that grants `view` to your GitHub user `navya-p`. Try `kubectl get pods -n redwood-app` now.

infra-bot: [system] rolebinding/redwood-app-view created by Priya Singh at 2026-03-23T12:34:50Z

Navya Patel: Running `kubectl get pods -n redwood-app` now returns the expected list. `kubectl logs -f` still dropped once but then stayed stable after I re-ran `./scripts/kube/login.sh navya-p` and `kubectl config use-context navya-redwood-app`. Much improved. Thanks!

Priya Singh: Great — if you still see flakes DM me and I'll grep the auth-proxy logs. Also adding a note to the onboarding doc: `/docs/onboarding/kube-sso.md` about running the helper script on mac M1.

Navya Patel: Will do, and I'll update my onboarding checklist. Thanks everyone :tada: :heart:
